headline: FIFA has still not said whose information was accessed or whether fans or ticket holders are affected.
summary: Re-read The Record's Nov 25 report: unchanged; FIFA did not answer follow-up questions. The Guardian's Nov 26 report could not be read (access blocked). No FIFA notice, newsroom statement or law-enforcement statement found on who is affected (q003), who did it (q002) or how much was taken (q005). Theory sweep: the only Hacker News thread on the incident (the Guardian link, Nov 27) has one comment and no theory; an older 99-comment FIFA thread is about a separate earlier flaw.
author: Research agent

headline: FIFA says a criminal cyberattack gave access to a limited set of personal and business information; it has not said who is affected.
summary: New incident page. FIFA's statement was sent separately to The Record (s001, Nov 25), Al Jazeera (s002) and The Associated Press (s003, both Nov 26); no notice on FIFA's own site was found, so the main answer rests on three independent outlets receiving the statement and is Confirmed, filed under hack-stated. incident_type breach: personal and business information was accessed. No service: nothing went down. The Handsome Boy Hacking Club's claim (12 GB, extortion, publication) is the group's own and Reported; the impersonation account (The Athletic's source) and the under-0.1-percent figure (Reuters' source) reach us through Al Jazeera and are Reported. Size Large rests on FIFA being football's world governing body; no count is known. incident_date is the day FIFA confirmed the attack; when it began is not known. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread about the incident; Reddit could not be read. Picture: a 2016 photograph of FIFA's Zurich headquarters from Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0); the 800-pixel copy was scaled from the 1920-pixel file because Commons refused the second request. Privacy check done: no staff, reporters or commenters named.
